message.description: git's first line, e.g. "fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/a/b.git/'"; "offline".

BaseErrorKind.description: Why a worktree's base may be behind its remote's default branch.

oneOf.description: The remote can't be reached, or didn't answer in time.
The remote refused git's credentials; the agent's pushes will fail the same way.
The remote says there is no such repository: a wrong URL or name, or credentials that can't see it.
git can't run ssh on the machine: it isn't installed. The doctor shows it; no attention item.
The remote answered but names no default branch: its HEAD points at a branch it doesn't have.
The project has no remote: the base is a local branch.
Any other fetch failure.

RecoveryMode.description: How a recovering task goes on.

oneOf.description: In its thread (`claude --resume`), with a note to continue.
Its context is full: `/compact` in its thread first, then the note.
In a new thread on its branch and worktree, with its brief and a handoff from the last one.

RunEnd.description: Why a run ended, so a node going away reads apart from a person stopping it. Set once the run is no longer active.

oneOf.description: The agent finished the turn.
Someone interrupted or stopped it: `RunInfo.endedBy` says who.
A steer cut it short at a tool boundary to take its own turn (`RunInfo.supersededBy`). Not a failure.
The node was stopping (SIGTERM) and cut it.
The node found it active on start: it died with the node process (crash, SIGKILL, power loss).
The machine slept and the agent's stream did not come back.
The agent's process exited or was killed with nobody asking; `failure` has the exit code or signal.
A usage, rate or pool limit; `failure.resetAt` says when to continue.
The conversation no longer fits in the model's context.
Any other failure; `failure.class` says which.
Set by the hub, never by a node: the watchdog saw no output for too long and ended the run.

base.description:
Where its worktree's branch started, as the node reported at launch; write tasks only, absent before a launch
or from an older node.

parked.description: M4: its thread hit a usage limit; the task is idle until fleetd sends "continue" at `resumeAt`.

paths.description: The files the lead said a writer will change (`spawn_agent` `paths`), matched against later work.

pr.description: The PR a review task reviews. Required at spawn for review; absent on older rows (hub-spawned judges).

previousThreads.description:
The threads it ran in before `threadRef`, oldest first: fleetd restarted it fresh (its context filled up, or its
thread could not resume), on the same branch and worktree.

profile.description: Resolved at spawn. Rows stored with a model and effort read as `high` (the hub migrates its own).

queuedReason.description: Why it is queued, e.g. "fleet cap: 40 of 40 running".

recovery.description: Set once a run of it died (its node stopped, its process was killed, a stall) and fleetd resumed it or will.

TaskKind.description: Every task gets its own worktree: a writer on its own branch, a reader or reviewer detached.

TaskProfile.description:
What an agent runs on. There are exactly two: `high` is the default and what the lead, every reviewer and every
helper call run; `medium` is for mechanical tasks the lead picks. The node's runner picks the model and effort of
each.

TaskRecovery.description: A task fleetd resumes on its own after its run died: in the same thread and worktree, with a note to continue.

count.description:
Automatic recoveries used of `max`; a resumed run that died again before doing anything counts twice. A node
going away never counts here.

lastCauseText.description: The same, in plain words: "the node on devbox stopped", "the agent was killed by signal 9".

nextAt.description: When the resume goes out; absent once it has.

nodeLost.description:
Resumes after its node went away (stopped, upgraded, crashed, powered off): not the task's doing, so outside
`count`, with a high ceiling of its own only so a node that keeps dying can't loop it forever.

resumedAt.description: When the last resume went out.

signature.description:
What tells one death from another (its cause, exit and last tool); the same one twice is not resumed again.
Cleared when the lead continues the task itself.

streak.description: Deaths in a row with this signature, the latest one included.

endCause.description:
Why its last run ended (the node stopped, the agent exited, a limit, context full, …); absent on results an
older hub recorded, and when it never ran.

tail.description: The latest assistant message, trimmed to its last 2000 characters.

UsageClass.description:
What stopped a turn. `usage_limit`: the plan's usage limit or a proxy cooldown, with a reset. `rate_limit`: a 429.
`pool_exhausted`: the user's proxy has no account for the model; it waits for usage_resume.

UsageParked.description: A task or lead whose thread hit a limit; fleetd sends it one "continue" at `resume_at`.

resumeAt.description: Absent for pool_exhausted: it resumes on usage_resume.

WorktreeBase.description: Where a writer's worktree branch started: the remote's default branch, freshly fetched unless `error` says why not.

fetchedAt.description:
When `ref` was last fetched: by this start, else by the one whose copy it fell back to. Absent for a local
branch, or when git can't tell.

forkBehind.description:
A fork (an `upstream` remote beside it) only: the commits upstream's default branch has that `ref` lacks, as
last fetched.

ref.description: "origin/main"; a local branch when there is no remote, or no copy of the remote's.
